problem: The company wanted to prevent others from offering Redis as a service without contributing back.
title: Redis changes its license in 2024, then adds AGPL in 2025
context: Redis was BSD licensed until it moved to source-available licences to limit cloud providers.
decision_made: Move from BSD to RSALv2 and SSPLv1 in March 2024.
action_taken: In May 2025 Redis 8 added the AGPLv3 open source licence as an option.
observed_outcome: The 2024 change triggered the Valkey fork. In 2025 Redis added AGPL, and critics said it might be too late or too restrictive.
lessons: Licence changes can fragment a community, and partial reversals may not restore trust.
limitations: Some sources describe the 2025 change as a full return and others as an added option. Long-term adoption effects are not documented.

claims.claim_text: Redis moved from BSD to more restrictive source-available licences in 2024.
Redis 8 added the AGPLv3 licence in May 2025, after the community had created the Valkey fork.
